title: Champions vs native Ascend aclnn (CANN 9.0.0), measured 2026-11-07

protocol.pypto_side: frozen remote_harness.py, latency_us = median per-round effective_us (PYPTO_BENCH=1)
protocol.aclnn_side: tools/aclnn_bench.py (pyacl + ctypes on libopapi.so): wall-clock per round (enqueue + acl.rt.synchronize_stream), median; executor fetched once and reused. Both sides end-to-end wall clock including host dispatch.
protocol.shape_policy: m-tier shape {M:4096, N:4096}; dtype = each champion's native contract dtype

aclnn_baseline_semantics: Our GEGLU computes gelu(g)*u on two full [M,N] tensors (tanh approx). aclnnGeGlu halves ONE tensor along a dim (different op semantics), so the native baseline is the unfused decomposition aclnnGeluV2(approximate=tanh) + aclnnMul — the composition a user would write without a fused kernel.

results.pypto_error: chip run lane poisoned: finalize_native_run failed with code 507901 (kernel launches row_blocks*col_blocks = 32768 spmd blocks at 4096x4096; reproducible on 2 attempts, other kernels pass on the same card in the same session)
results.note: e000005 was crowned in the s-tier fp32 campaign (dispatch-bound small shapes); it does not launch at m-tier and is far off aclnn at 2048x2048. Recorded as-is.
same aclnn bf16 run as e000013's row (identical shape/dtype).

convention: speedup_pypto_vs_aclnn = aclnn_us / pypto_us; >1 means the pypto champion is faster
